t:
(a) Definition.—In this Act, the term “covered employee” means—
        (1) an employee whose pay is disbursed by the Secretary of the Senate; or 
        (2) any other individual who is authorized to park in any parking area under the jurisdiction of the Senate on Capitol Grounds.  
    (b) Authority.—
        (1) In general.—Subject to paragraph (3), funds appropriated to the Architect of the Capitol under the heading “Capitol Power Plant” under the heading “ARCHITECT OF THE CAPITOL” in any fiscal year are available to construct, operate, and maintain on a reimbursable basis battery recharging stations in parking areas under the jurisdiction of the Senate on Capitol Grounds for use by privately owned vehicles used by Senators or covered employees. 
        (2) Vendors authorized.—In carrying out paragraph (1), the Architect of the Capitol may use 1 or more vendors on a commission basis. 
        (3) Approval of construction.—The Architect of the Capitol may construct or direct the construction of battery recharging stations described under paragraph (1) after—
            (A) submission of written notice detailing the numbers and locations of the battery recharging stations to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate; and 
            (B) approval by that Committee.   
    (c) Fees and Charges.—
        (1) In general.—Subject to paragraph (2), the Architect of the Capitol shall charge fees or charges for electricity provided to Senators and covered employees sufficient to cover the costs to the Architect of the Capitol to carry out this section, including costs to any vendors or other costs associated with maintaining the battery recharging stations. 
        (2) Approval of fees or charges.—The Architect of the Capitol may establish and adjust fees or charges under paragraph (1) after—
            (A) submission of written notice detailing the amount of the fee or charge to be established or adjusted to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate; and 
            (B) approval by that Committee.   
    (d) Deposit and Availability of Fees, Charges, and Commissions.—Any fees, charges, or commissions collected by the Architect of the Capitol under this section shall be—
        (1) deposited in the Treasury to the credit of the appropriations account described under subsection (b); and 
        (2) available for obligation without further appropriation during—
            (A) the fiscal year collected; and 
            (B) the fiscal year following the fiscal year collected.   
    (e) Reports.—
        (1) In general.—Not later than 30 days after the end of each fiscal year, the Architect of the Capitol shall submit a report on the financial administration and cost recovery of activities under this section with respect to that fiscal year to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate. 
        (2) Avoiding subsidy.—
            (A) Determination.—Not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act and every 3 years thereafter, the Architect of the Capitol shall submit a report to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate determining whether Senators and covered employees using battery charging stations as authorized by this Act are receiving a subsidy from the taxpayers. 
            (B) Modification of rates and fees.—If a determination is made under subparagraph (A) that a subsidy is being received, the Architect of the Capitol shall submit a plan to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate on how to update the program to ensure no subsidy is being received. If the committee does not act on the plan within 60 days, the Architect of the Capitol shall take appropriate steps to increase rates or fees to ensure reimbursement for the cost of the program consistent with an appropriate schedule for amortization, to be charged to those using the charging stations.   
    (f) Effective Date.—This Act shall apply with respect to fiscal year 2011 and each fiscal year thereafter.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the notice, approval, and reporting requirements are participation, but every one of them runs between the Architect of the Capitol and a Senate committee, both inside the federal government. The only outside parties are vendors used on a commission basis, which is a contracting arrangement and not consultation on a federal decision. The section provides no public comment, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body with outside members, or right to sue.
fable.s: submission of written notice detailing the numbers and locations of the battery recharging stations to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Architect of the Capitol to submit notices and obtain approval from the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration. The Senate is part of the federal government (legislative branch), so this interaction is internal to the government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with entities outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private organizations.
qwen_block.s: The Architect of the Capitol may construct or direct the construction of battery recharging stations described under paragraph (1) after— (A) submission of written notice detailing the numbers and locations of the battery recharging stations to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate; and (B) approval by that Committee.

opus.w: Every required notice, approval, report and plan runs between the Architect of the Capitol and the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, and both are inside the federal government. That makes this intra-government coordination, not outside participation. The use of vendors on a commission basis is a contracting arrangement, which the definition excludes. No state, member of the public, expert or other outside party takes part in any decision.

opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section requires written notice to the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration and that Committee's approval before any construction or fee change. It also requires recurring reports and plans. But the Architect of the Capitol and the Senate Committee are both inside the federal government, so this is all internal coordination. The authority to use "vendors on a commission basis" is a contracting arrangement, not outside participation in the decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Architect of the Capitol to submit notices and obtain approval from the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate. Both the Architect of the Capitol and the Senate Committee are part of the federal government (specifically the legislative branch). Therefore, this interaction is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by parties outside the federal government. The definition explicitly states that Congress and its committees are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: (3) Approval of construction.—The Architect of the Capitol may construct or direct the construction of battery recharging stations described under paragraph (1) after— (A) submission of written notice detailing the numbers and locations of the battery recharging stations to the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate; and (B) approval by that Committee.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "covered employees" (who are Senate employees) or the vendors involved constitute "people outside of the government" participating in the decision. However, Senate employees are part of the legislative branch of the federal government, and vendors are merely service providers, not participants in the decision-making process itself. The key interactions described are between the Architect of the Capitol (an officer of the legislative branch) and the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate (a committee of Congress). Since both entities are inside the federal government, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outsiders.
